questions.question: A server refuses a request that is over the limit with the HTTP status code _____.
questions.explanation: It means "Too Many Requests" and tells the client to slow down and try again later.

questions.question: Why would a public contact form need a rate limit?
questions.answer: Without one, a bot could send thousands of messages, flooding the inbox and using up any paid or free quota.
questions.explanation: The limit caps how much damage one sender can do.

questions.question: What does the key of a rate limiter decide?
options: How long the time window lasts
Which requests share the same counter
questions.explanation: The key (an account, an IP address, a network) groups requests: the same key means the same counter. B is the limit itself, not the key.

questions.question: The limit is 3 messages per 10 minutes, with a sliding window. Messages were sent at minutes 0, 2 and 4. When can the next one go through?
questions.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 90" role="img" aria-label="A timeline from minute 0 to 15 with messages at minutes 0, 2 and 4"><line x1="20" y1="45" x2="280" y2="45" stroke="#8a94a3" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="20" y1="38" x2="20" y2="52" stroke="#8a94a3" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="105" y1="38" x2="105" y2="52" stroke="#8a94a3" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="190" y1="38" x2="190" y2="52" stroke="#8a94a3" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="275" y1="38" x2="275" y2="52" stroke="#8a94a3" stroke-width="2"/><text x="20" y="72" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">0</text><text x="105" y="72" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">5</text><text x="190" y="72" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">10</text><text x="275" y="72" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">15 min</text><circle cx="20" cy="45" r="7" fill="#5b7fe0"/><circle cx="54" cy="45" r="7" fill="#5b7fe0"/><circle cx="88" cy="45" r="7" fill="#5b7fe0"/><text x="54" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#5b7fe0">3 messages</text></svg>
questions.explanation: Just after minute 10, the message from minute 0 leaves the 10-minute window, so only 2 are counted. C is tempting, but you don't wait for all three to expire, only the oldest.

questions.question: Is it true that a fixed window can let through almost twice the limit in a short time?
questions.explanation: A visitor can use the full limit just before the reset and again just after it. A sliding window avoids this.

questions.question: In a token bucket, each request spends one _____, and they refill slowly over time.
questions.explanation: When the bucket is empty, requests are refused until it refills.

questions.question: Is it true that a token bucket forbids all bursts of requests?
questions.explanation: A full bucket allows a short burst (spend all tokens at once); it only limits the average rate over time.

questions.question: Why group visitors by network instead of by their exact IP address?
questions.answer: One person often controls many addresses in the same block and can switch between them.
questions.explanation: Grouping by network stops them from getting a fresh limit each time.

questions.question: Is it true that a server can safely trust the first address in the X-Forwarded-For header?
questions.explanation: The visitor can write anything at the start of that header. Only the entry added by your own proxy (the last one, on Render) can be trusted.

questions.question: Why must the memory of a rate limiter be bounded?
options: To make the code easier to read
Because limits must reset every hour
Because a dictionary cannot hold many entries
Because requests from many addresses could fill memory until the server crashes
questions.explanation: Every new key adds an entry. Without a maximum, an attacker using many addresses could grow memory forever. C is wrong: dictionaries can grow very large, which is exactly the danger.

questions.question: A bug where parallel requests interfere and the result depends on who goes first is a race _____.
questions.explanation: In a rate limiter, several requests can all pass the check before any of them is counted.

questions.question: How does a lock fix the race condition in a rate limiter?
questions.answer: It lets only one request at a time check the counter and count itself, in one step.
questions.explanation: The next request then sees the updated count, so no extra request slips through.

questions.question: Why should a message that failed to send still count against the limit?
options: So retrying can't be used to send unlimited requests
Because failed requests are always attacks
To make the error message shorter
Because the server cannot tell it failed
questions.explanation: Otherwise someone could retry forever. Also, a timeout may have delivered the email anyway. B is too strong: honest sends fail too.

questions.question: Is it true that a global limit can block honest visitors if an attacker uses it up?
questions.explanation: The global cap is shared by everyone. It protects the inbox and quota, but the price is that a flood can make the form unavailable for a while.
